chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi'za from Abu Basir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If you saw me while I was on the bank of the Euphrates praying and I was fearing the wild beasts,' he said to me, 'Why did you not pray while you were riding?'

key_terms.اَلسَّبُع: Wild beasts or animals, referring to potential danger
key_terms.اَلْفُرَات: The Euphrates River, a major geographical landmark in Iraq
key_terms.رَاكِبٌ: Riding or mounted, referring to the posture of prayer while on an animal

ai.seo_question: How should one pray when fearing danger or hardship while traveling?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the concession for praying while riding applies not only to the specific context of battle (*salat al-khawf*) but also to general travel where fear of danger, such as wild beasts, exists. This establishes a broader principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the preservation of safety and ease over rigid ritual form when circumstances warrant. The ruling underscores the pragmatic nature of Shia fiqh, where the intent of the lawgiver accommodates the physical reality of the worshipper.
